problem: Existing telepresence robots rely on manual navigation, which is tedious in unfamiliar remote places, and their software is tightly coupled to specific robot hardware. Prior embodied-AI work also has no concrete definition, benchmark or method for AreaGoal navigation (going to a region such as 'bedroom').
motivation: Remote caregiving, for example for isolated or elderly patients, needs non-expert operators to command a robot with high-level speech rather than continuous joystick control. The paper therefore builds a hardware-agnostic edge-cloud telepresence system that integrates embodied-AI navigation, dialogue and person following.
key_idea: Build a loosely coupled, ROS-based, WebRTC/edge telepresence system whose speech commands invoke PointGoal, ObjectGoal and a newly defined AreaGoal navigation, the latter using object-region relation graphs, opening detection and grid-map backtracking, plus person following.
insight: AreaGoal can be solved in a modular, training-light way by combining object-to-region probabilities, region transition priors, opening detection and landmark backtracking. Ablations reported in text (no numbers) show that manual survey-based relation weights beat weights learned from random walks, and that GCN embeddings help ObjectGoal but not AreaGoal. The modular PointNav stack (mapper, A*, heuristic local policy) is claimed to support sim-to-real transfer without retraining.
method: System architecture: four subsystems (Communication, Embodied Dialogue, Embodied Navigation, UI) across master device, cloud, robot and robot-edge. Uses a hybrid WebRTC topology (SRTP star for A/V, P2P SCTP for control) and WebSocket offloading of computation to the edge, on ROS 1 or ROS 2.
HRI module: a CNN command-word detector plus VAD, then a wav2vec-based ASR, then a task identifier that extracts the task and parameters. Ambiguity triggers a question back to the operator.

PointNav module: depth is projected to an egocentric occupancy map, a spatial transform builds the global map, a modified A* with obstacle-weighted costs plans the path, and a heuristic local policy chooses forward/left/right.

ObjectNav module: a 3-layer GCN over a Spatial Relational Graph of objects and regions (Visual Genome plus random-walk weights) produces 128-d embeddings. A similarity score of the current walk against successful walks guides search, executed by a shortest-path follower.

AreaNav module: YOLO object detection (with extra open door, closed door and free-area classes) and a region relation graph give the current-region probability. A region transition graph, opening detection (YOLO or depth contours), mirror avoidance, an object-to-PointGoal mapper and a grid-map Visual Semantic Map with landmark backtracking and corner fallback complete the module. Rotations are triggered adaptively.

Person following: YOLO detection plus a user-tagged target. GOTURN, CSRT and an online one-class SVM re-identifier vote on the target, and the robot moves left/forward/right by bbox overlap and stops when the bbox is large.

Browser UI and user study: a responsive web UI with manual, map, AR-pin and speech control and multi-party control handoff. A 30-user study rated features on a 1-5 scale, aggregated into an importance-weighted MOS.

setting.backbone: Modular: YOLO detector (extra 3 classes), wav2vec ASR, CNN command-word classifier, 3-layer GCN (ObjectNav), GOTURN/CSRT/one-class SVM (person following), A* + heuristic policy (PointNav)
setting.training_data: GCN trained on Visual Genome relations plus random-walk exploration in many AI Habitat scenes; YOLO extended with 100 manually annotated images per class for door/free-area; ASR is an in-house wav2vec adaptation; AreaNav relation weights come from a manual user survey
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D plus wheel odometry (ground-truth pose in simulation evaluation)
setting.action_space: Discrete: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30° (Habitat); finer angle/step on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson for PointNav, Matterport3D for ObjectNav/AreaNav); Webots for person following
setting.privileged: Ground-truth pose for PointNav evaluation; ground-truth region boundaries used to define AreaGoal success on MP3D

numbers_note: Benchmarks are non-standard (own AreaGoal tasks); the ObjectNav and AreaGoal splits are unspecified, so 'val' is a guess. User-study results are only in figures.
results: On the AreaGoal task the method averages 0.942 success and 182 steps, versus 0.875 / 221 for frontier-based exploration and 0.725 / 361 for random. Gains are largest on study room (0.85 vs 0.65). ObjectGoal reaches 0.941 success and 0.658 SPL versus 0.598 / 0.370 for frontier exploration. PointNav reaches 91.05% on Gibson.
limitations: Baselines are weak (random and frontier only), with no comparison to learned ObjectNav/AreaNav methods (SemExp is mentioned but not tabulated); the evaluation is on small subsets with ambiguous splits.
Real-robot results are qualitative only (no quantitative PointNav or AreaGoal real-world evaluation); CenterAreaGoal is left out of scope; the code is not released.
AreaNav relies on hand-tuned heuristics and survey-based weights, and evaluation uses ground-truth pose and region boundaries.
compares_to: Existing telepresence systems (Double, Temi, ENRICHME, etc.)
